```{python}
import json
from html import escape

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display
from itables import init_notebook_mode, show

from pdi import site
from pdi.tech_value import dashboard

# Bundle the table script into the page instead of loading it from a CDN.
init_notebook_mode(connected=False)

parts, meta = site.load("tech-value", "fair_price")
board, board_meta = site.load("tech-value", "fair_price_leaderboard")
history, _ = site.load("tech-value", "price_history")
verdicts = meta.get("verdicts") or {}
KINDS = {"gpu": "Graphics cards", "cpu": "Processors"}
SHORT = {"gpu": "GPU", "cpu": "CPU"}
NEAR_PCT = 10.0  # within +/- this of the estimate reads as "near fair"
GAP_COLORS = {"under": "#18b47b", "near": "#f5b400", "above": "#ef5b4c"}
MAKER_COLORS = {"NVIDIA": "#2a78d6", "AMD": "#3aa63a", "Intel": "#9b5de5", "Other": "#9aa3ad"}
REGIME_CURVES = {
    "Consumer / Mainstream": ("P50 (mainstream regime)", "Typical price curve for mainstream {noun}", "#2a78d6"),
    "Workstation / Pro": ("P50 (workstation regime)", "Typical price curve for workstation-class {noun}", "#f0a500"),
    "3D V-Cache (X3D)": ("P50 (X3D regime)", "Typical price curve for 3D V-Cache (X3D) {noun}", "#ef5b4c"),
}
NOUN = {"gpu": "GPUs", "cpu": "CPUs"}

_P = {
    "chip": '<rect x="6" y="6" width="12" height="12" rx="2"/><rect x="9" y="9" width="6" height="6"/><path d="M9 2v4M15 2v4M9 18v4M15 18v4M2 9h4M2 15h4M18 9h4M18 15h4"/>',
    "gpu": '<rect x="2" y="6" width="20" height="12" rx="2"/><circle cx="8.5" cy="12" r="3"/><circle cx="15.5" cy="12" r="3"/><path d="M4 18v2M20 6V4"/>',
    "bars": '<path d="M5 20V12M12 20V5M19 20v-9"/>',
    "target": '<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.5"/>',
    "diamond": '<path d="M12 3l9 9-9 9-9-9z"/><path d="M8 12h8"/>',
    "trend": '<path d="M3 17l6-6 4 4 8-8"/><path d="M15 7h6v6"/>',
    "layers": '<path d="M12 3l9 5-9 5-9-5z"/><path d="M3 13l9 5 9-5"/><path d="M3 17.5l9 5 9-5" opacity=".6"/>',
    "check": '<path d="M5 12.5l4.5 4.5L19 7.5"/>',
    "shield": '<path d="M12 3l8 3v6c0 4.5-3.4 8-8 9-4.6-1-8-4.5-8-9V6z"/><path d="M8.5 12l2.5 2.5 4.5-5"/>',
    "trophy": '<path d="M7 4h10v5a5 5 0 01-10 0z"/><path d="M7 6H4a3 3 0 003 4M17 6h3a3 3 0 01-3 4M12 14v4M8 21h8M9 18h6"/>',
    "info": '<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 11v6M12 7.5v.5"/>',
    "chev": '<path d="M6 9l6 6 6-6"/>',
}


def icon(name: str, cls: str = "") -> str:
    return f'<svg class="fp-ico {cls}" viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">{_P[name]}</svg>'


def maker(key: str) -> str:
    name = dashboard.display_name(str(key).split()[0]) if key else ""
    return name if name in MAKER_COLORS else "Other"


def band(gap: float) -> str:
    return "under" if gap <= -NEAR_PCT else ("above" if gap >= NEAR_PCT else "near")


def prepare(kind: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    part = parts[parts["kind"] == kind].copy() if len(parts) else parts
    if part.empty:
        return part
    part["display_model"] = part["model_key"].map(dashboard.display_name)
    part["maker"] = part["model_key"].map(maker)
    part["gap_band"] = part["gap_pct"].map(band)
    for col, default in {
        "regime": "Consumer / Mainstream",
        "blocking_rival": "On Pareto frontier",
        "ensemble_price_usd": None,
        "floor_p20_usd": None,
        "ceiling_p80_usd": None,
    }.items():
        if col not in part.columns:
            part[col] = part["fair_price_usd"] if default is None else default
    for col in ("model_disagreement_pct", "listing_spread_pct", "source_spread_pct",
                "drop_to_frontier_usd", "drop_to_frontier_pct", "drop_to_best_value_pct",
                "price_change_7d_pct"):
        if col not in part.columns:
            part[col] = 0.0
    for col in ("channel_signal", "lifecycle_signal"):
        if col not in part.columns:
            part[col] = ""
    return part


groups = {kind: prepare(kind) for kind in KINDS}


def fmt_usd(v: float) -> str:
    return f"${v:,.0f}"


def gap_phrase(gap: float) -> str:
    if abs(gap) < 0.5:
        return "in line with estimate"
    return f"{abs(gap):.0f}% {'below' if gap < 0 else 'above'} estimate"


def typical_errors(kind: str):
    """Typical out-of-sample error (median absolute % error) of the baseline and the pick."""
    if board.empty:
        return None, None
    b = board[board["kind"] == kind]
    base = b[b.get("is_baseline", False) == True]  # noqa: E712
    used = b[b["used"] == True]  # noqa: E712
    if base.empty or used.empty:
        return None, None
    return float(base["median_abs_pct_error"].iloc[0]), float(used["median_abs_pct_error"].iloc[0])


def agreement(kind: str) -> float | None:
    part = groups[kind]
    if part.empty:
        return None
    trained = part[part["n_listings"] >= 2]
    spread = (trained if len(trained) else part)["model_disagreement_pct"].median()
    return max(0.0, 1 - spread / 100)


def confidence_label(score: float | None) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    if score is None:
        return "Unknown", "fp-pill-mod", "no model results yet"
    if score >= 0.90:
        return "High", "fp-pill-neg", "stable fit"
    if score >= 0.80:
        return "Moderate", "fp-pill-mod", "some disagreement between the top models"
    return "Low", "fp-pill-pos", "the top models disagree; treat estimates with care"


def price_change(kind: str):
    """Median change in each part's lowest price over the last 30 days of collected history."""
    if history.empty:
        return None, None
    h = history[history["kind"] == kind].copy()
    if h.empty:
        return None, None
    h["date"] = pd.to_datetime(h["date"])
    latest = h["date"].max()
    window = h[h["date"] >= latest - pd.Timedelta(days=30)].sort_values("date")
    first = window.groupby("model_key").first()
    last = window.groupby("model_key").last()
    ok = (last.index.isin(first.index)) & (first["date"] < last["date"])
    if not ok.any():
        return None, None
    chg = (last.loc[ok, "price_usd"] / first.loc[ok, "price_usd"] - 1) * 100
    span = int((latest - window["date"].min()).days)
    return float(chg.median()), span
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"""
<header class="fp-bar">
  <div class="fp-brand">{icon("chip")}<span>Tech Value: <em>Fair Price</em></span></div>
  <div class="fp-sub">PC Parts Research Dashboard</div>
  <div class="fp-chips"><span>{icon("bars")}Data-driven</span><span>{icon("target")}Fair price</span><span>{icon("layers")}GPU &amp; CPU</span></div>
</header>

<div class="fp-head">
<h1>Which parts cost less, or more, than their benchmark performance predicts</h1>
<p>We estimate a &ldquo;fair price&rdquo; for each part from its benchmark performance using fitted price&ndash;performance models (an ensemble of top models).
The gap shows how the listing compares to the estimated price: a <span class="fp-pill fp-pill-neg">negative gap</span> means the listing is below the estimated price (cheaper than expected
for its performance), while a <span class="fp-pill fp-pill-pos">positive gap</span> means it is above the estimate (more expensive than expected).</p>
</div>
""")

cards = []
for kind, label in KINDS.items():
    v = verdicts.get(kind) or {}
    base, best = typical_errors(kind)
    beats = bool(v.get("beats_baseline"))
    if not v:
        badge = '<span class="fp-badge fp-badge-off">Awaiting results</span>'
        body = "No model result is available yet."
    elif beats:
        badge = f'<span class="fp-badge">{icon("check")}Beats baseline</span>'
        body = "Our best fitted model beats the naive baseline (simple global price-per-performance)"
        body += f" by ~{(base - best) / base * 100:.0f}% lower typical error (MAPE)." if base and best else "."
    else:
        badge = '<span class="fp-badge fp-badge-off">Baseline retained</span>'
        body = "No fitted model beat the naive baseline (simple global price-per-performance) clearly enough, so the baseline sets the fair price."
    if base and best:
        body += f" Typical error {best:.0f}% vs. {base:.0f}% for the baseline."
    score = agreement(kind)
    conf, tone, why = confidence_label(score)
    agree = f"ensemble agreement {score:.2f}, {why}" if score is not None else why
    cards.append(f"""<article class="fp-verdict" data-tone="{kind}">{icon(kind if kind == "gpu" else "chip")}
<div><div class="fp-verdict-top"><h2>{label}</h2>{badge}</div>
<p>{escape(body)}</p>
<p>Model confidence: <span class="fp-pill {tone}">{conf}</span> ({agree}).</p></div></article>""")
print('<div class="fp-verdicts">' + "".join(cards) + "</div>")


def pct(value, fmt=".0f", sign=False):
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and np.isnan(value)):
        return "—"
    return format(value, ("+" if sign else "") + fmt) + "%"


for kind in KINDS:
    part = groups[kind]
    v = verdicts.get(kind) or {}
    multi = part[part["n_listings"] >= 2] if not part.empty else part
    spread = multi["listing_spread_pct"].median() if len(multi) else None
    frontier = part["drop_to_frontier_pct"].median() if len(part) else None
    change, span = price_change(kind)
    change_note = "Median price vs. 30 days ago" if span and span >= 30 else (
        f"Median price vs. {span} days ago (history so far)" if span else "Not enough price history yet")
    cover = v.get("p20_p80_loo_coverage_pct")
    target = v.get("p20_p80_target_coverage_pct", 60)
    cover_cls = "fp-warn" if cover is not None and cover < target else ""
    print(f"""<section class="fp-watch" data-kind="{kind}">
<div class="fp-watch-title">{icon("bars")}<div><b>Market watch</b><small>Current market conditions (new listings), {KINDS[kind].lower()}</small></div></div>
<div><h4>{icon("diamond")}Seller spread</h4><strong>{pct(spread)}</strong><small>Cheapest listing below the median listing, typical part</small></div>
<div><h4>{icon("target")}Frontier distance</h4><strong>{pct(frontier)}</strong><small>Typical gap to the best price&ndash;performance listings</small></div>
<div><h4>{icon("trend")}Price change</h4><strong>{pct(change, ".1f", sign=True)}</strong><small>{change_note}</small></div>
<div><h4>{icon("layers")}P20&ndash;P80 coverage</h4><strong class="{cover_cls}">{pct(cover)}</strong><small>Of held-out parts fall within the model&rsquo;s P20&ndash;P80 band ({target:.0f}% target)</small></div>
</section>""")
```

```{python}
def smooth(x, y, deg=2, n=80, lo=None, hi=None):
    """A smooth display curve through per-part estimates, fitted in log-log space."""
    lx, ly = np.log10(np.asarray(x, float)), np.log10(np.asarray(y, float))
    ok = np.isfinite(lx) & np.isfinite(ly)
    lx, ly = lx[ok], ly[ok]
    if len(lx) < 2:
        return None, None
    deg = min(deg, len(np.unique(lx)) - 1, 1 if len(lx) < 8 else deg)
    coef = np.polyfit(lx, ly, deg)
    grid = np.linspace(lo if lo is not None else lx.min(), hi if hi is not None else lx.max(), n)
    return 10 ** grid, 10 ** np.polyval(coef, grid)


def log_ticks(lo, hi, steps=(1, 2, 5)):
    vals = [m * 10 ** e for e in range(int(np.floor(np.log10(lo))), int(np.ceil(np.log10(hi))) + 1) for m in steps]
    return [v for v in vals if lo / 1.05 <= v <= hi * 1.05]


SUP = str.maketrans("0123456789-", "⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹⁻")


def chart(kind, part):
    fig = go.Figure()
    lx = np.log10(part["score"])
    lo, hi = lx.min(), lx.max()
    bx, low = smooth(part["score"], part["floor_p20_usd"])
    _, high = smooth(part["score"], part["ceiling_p80_usd"])
    if bx is not None:
        fig.add_scatter(x=bx, y=low, mode="lines", line=dict(width=0), hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False)
        fig.add_scatter(x=bx, y=high, mode="lines", line=dict(width=0), fill="tonexty",
                        fillcolor="rgba(24,180,123,0.20)", hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False)
    for regime, (name, _, color) in REGIME_CURVES.items():
        grp = part[part["regime"] == regime]
        if len(grp) < 2:
            continue
        rx, ry = smooth(grp["score"], grp["fair_price_usd"])
        if rx is not None:
            fig.add_scatter(x=rx, y=ry, mode="lines", line=dict(dash="dash", width=2.2, color=color),
                            hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False)
    ex, ey = smooth(part["score"], part["ensemble_price_usd"])
    if ex is not None:
        fig.add_scatter(x=ex, y=ey, mode="lines", line=dict(width=2.6, color="#0f8f6c"),
                        hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False)
    custom = np.stack([
        part["display_model"], part["fair_price_usd"], part["gap_pct"], part["n_listings"],
        part["regime"], part["floor_p20_usd"], part["ceiling_p80_usd"],
    ], axis=-1)
    hover = ("<b>%{customdata[0]}</b><br>Listed $%{y:,.0f} · estimated $%{customdata[1]:,.0f}"
             "<br>Gap %{customdata[2]:+.0f}% · %{customdata[3]} listing(s)"
             "<br>P20–P80 $%{customdata[5]:,.0f} – $%{customdata[6]:,.0f}<br>%{customdata[4]}<extra></extra>")
    # Two colourings of the same points; the legend switches between them.
    for mode, column, palette in (("gap", "gap_band", GAP_COLORS), ("maker", "maker", MAKER_COLORS)):
        for key, color in palette.items():
            mask = (part[column] == key).to_numpy()
            if not mask.any():
                continue
            fig.add_scatter(
                x=part["score"][mask], y=part["price_usd"][mask], mode="markers",
                marker=dict(size=9, color=color, line=dict(width=1, color="rgba(255,255,255,0.85)")),
                customdata=custom[mask], hovertemplate=hover, name=f"{mode}:{key}",
                visible=(mode == "gap"), showlegend=False,
            )
    # Highlight for the selected part; the script below moves it.
    fig.add_scatter(x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers", name="selected", hoverinfo="skip", showlegend=False,
                    marker=dict(size=18, color="rgba(24,180,123,0.25)", line=dict(width=2.5, color="#0f8f6c")))
    ylo = min(part["price_usd"].min(), part["floor_p20_usd"].min())
    yhi = max(part["price_usd"].max(), part["ceiling_p80_usd"].max())
    yt = log_ticks(ylo, yhi)
    xt = [10 ** e for e in range(int(np.floor(lo)), int(np.ceil(hi)) + 1)]
    xt = [t for t in xt if lo - 0.05 <= np.log10(t) <= hi + 0.05]
    if len(xt) >= 2:
        xtext = [f"10{str(int(np.log10(t))).translate(SUP)}" for t in xt]
    else:  # less than two decades of scores: label 1-2-5 steps instead
        xt = log_ticks(10 ** lo, 10 ** hi)
        xtext = [f"{t:,.0f}" for t in xt]
    fig.update_layout(
        height=500,
        font=dict(family="Inter, Segoe UI, system-ui, sans-serif", color="#8391a1", size=13),
        margin=dict(t=14, r=12, b=56, l=78),
        paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
        xaxis=dict(type="log", showgrid=False, showline=True, linecolor="#8391a1", ticks="outside",
                   tickvals=xt, ticktext=xtext,
                   title="Blender benchmark score (higher is better, log scale)",
                   range=[lo - 0.05, hi + 0.05]),
        yaxis=dict(type="log", showgrid=False, showline=True, linecolor="#8391a1", ticks="outside",
                   tickvals=yt, ticktext=[f"{t:,.0f}" for t in yt],
                   title="Lowest new listing price (USD)",
                   range=[np.log10(ylo) - 0.06, np.log10(yhi) + 0.06]),
        hoverlabel=dict(bgcolor="white", font_color="#14233a"),
        dragmode=False,
    )
    fig.show(config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": True})


def legend(kind, part):
    regimes = [r for r in REGIME_CURVES if (part["regime"] == r).sum() >= 2]
    makers = [m for m in MAKER_COLORS if (part["maker"] == m).any()]
    gap_items = [
        ("under", "Under fair (≤ −10%)", "cheaper than estimate"),
        ("near", "Near fair (−10% to +10%)", "in line with estimate"),
        ("above", "Above fair (≥ +10%)", "more expensive than estimate"),
    ]
    rows = "".join(f'<li><span class="fp-dot" style="background:{GAP_COLORS[k]}"></span><span>{a} — <small style="display:inline">{b}</small></span></li>' for k, a, b in gap_items)
    makers_html = "".join(f'<li><span class="fp-dot" style="background:{MAKER_COLORS[m]}"></span>{m}</li>' for m in makers)
    curves = '<li><span class="fp-line" style="border-color:#0f8f6c"></span><span>Top-3 ensemble (fair price)<small>Ensemble of the 3 best-fitting models</small></span></li>'
    for r in regimes:
        name, note, color = REGIME_CURVES[r]
        curves += f'<li><span class="fp-line dash" style="border-color:{color}"></span><span>{name}<small>{note.format(noun=NOUN[kind])}</small></span></li>'
    curves += '<li><span class="fp-swatch"></span><span>P20–P80 coverage<small>Estimated typical price range (20th–80th percentile)</small></span></li>'
    print(f"""<aside class="fp-legend"><h3>Legend</h3>
<button type="button" data-color="gap" aria-pressed="true">Listing vs. fair price (gap)</button><ul data-legend="gap">{rows}</ul>
<button type="button" data-color="maker" aria-pressed="false">Maker (point color)</button><ul class="fp-inline fp-off" data-legend="maker">{makers_html}</ul>
<h4>Model &amp; price curves</h4><ul>{curves}</ul></aside>""")


def selection_data(part):
    rows = []
    for r in part.itertuples():
        trusted = r.n_listings >= 2
        rival = "" if str(r.blocking_rival) in ("", "On Pareto frontier") else dashboard.display_name(r.blocking_rival)
        if r.n_retailers >= 2:
            spread, spread_note = f"{r.source_spread_pct:.0f}%", f"Cheapest vs. median of {r.n_retailers} sellers"
        elif trusted:
            spread, spread_note = f"{r.listing_spread_pct:.0f}%", f"Cheapest vs. median of {r.n_listings} listings, one seller"
        else:
            spread, spread_note = "—", "Only one listing, no spread to measure"
        rows.append(dict(
            name=r.display_model, x=float(r.score), y=float(r.price_usd), est=round(float(r.fair_price_usd)),
            gap=round(float(r.gap_pct), 1), n=int(r.n_listings), trusted=bool(trusted),
            p20=round(float(r.floor_p20_usd)), p80=round(float(r.ceiling_p80_usd)),
            spread=spread, spread_note=spread_note,
            drop=round(float(r.drop_to_frontier_usd)), rival=rival,
        ))
    return rows


def picked_default(part):
    trusted = part[part["n_listings"] >= 2]
    return (trusted if len(trusted) else part).sort_values("gap_pct").iloc[0]["display_model"]


def selected(kind, part):
    rows = sorted(selection_data(part), key=lambda d: d["name"])
    opts = "".join(f'<option{" selected" if d["name"] == picked_default(part) else ""}>{escape(d["name"])}</option>' for d in rows)
    data = escape(json.dumps(rows), quote=True)
    print(f"""<div class="fp-pick" data-parts="{data}">{icon(kind if kind == "gpu" else "chip")}
<div class="fp-pick-main"><div class="fp-pick-title"></div><div class="fp-pick-note"></div></div>
<label>Inspect a part<br><select aria-label="Inspect a part">{opts}</select></label></div>
<div class="fp-tiles">
<div>{icon("target")}<div><span>Market position</span><strong data-f="pos"></strong><small>Listing vs. estimated typical price</small></div></div>
<div>{icon("bars")}<div><span>Median range</span><strong data-f="range"></strong><small>Estimated typical price range (P20–P80)</small></div></div>
<div>{icon("diamond")}<div><span>Spread (source)</span><strong data-f="spread"></strong><small data-f="spread_note"></small></div></div>
<div>{icon("shield")}<div><span>Pareto drop</span><strong data-f="drop"></strong><small data-f="drop_note"></small></div></div>
</div>""")


def panel(kind):
    part = groups[kind]
    print(f'<div class="fp-panel-head"><h2>{KINDS[kind]}: listing price vs. benchmark performance</h2>'
          "<p>Lowest new listing price vs. Blender benchmark score (log–log). Fair price is from an ensemble of "
          "fitted models, with P20–P80 coverage showing the typical price range for a given performance. "
          "Click a point to inspect it.</p></div>")
```

```{python}
def estimates(part):
    names = {m["id"]: m["name"] for m in meta.get("sources", [])}
    spread_col = [
        f"{sp:.1f}% ({nr} src)" if nr >= 2 else (f"{lp:.1f}% (1 src)" if nl >= 2 else "1 listing")
        for sp, lp, nr, nl in zip(part["source_spread_pct"], part["listing_spread_pct"],
                                  part["n_retailers"], part["n_listings"])
    ]
    frontier_col = [
        "On frontier ($0)" if d_usd <= 0
        else f"-${d_usd:,.0f} (-{d_pct:.1f}%) vs {dashboard.display_name(riv)}"
        for d_usd, d_pct, riv in zip(part["drop_to_frontier_usd"], part["drop_to_frontier_pct"],
                                     part["blocking_rival"])
    ]
    table = part.assign(
        Spread=spread_col,
        Frontier=frontier_col,
        Cheapest=[
            f'<a href="{url}">{names.get(key, key)}</a>' if url else names.get(key, key)
            for key, url in zip(part["retailer"], part["listing_url"])
        ],
    )[[
        "display_model", "maker", "regime", "gap_pct", "price_usd", "fair_price_usd",
        "ensemble_price_usd", "floor_p20_usd", "ceiling_p80_usd", "Spread", "Frontier",
        "price_change_7d_pct", "model_disagreement_pct", "n_listings", "Cheapest",
    ]].rename(columns={
        "display_model": "Model", "maker": "Maker", "regime": "Regime", "gap_pct": "Gap (%)",
        "price_usd": "Lowest (USD)", "fair_price_usd": "Estimated typical (USD)",
        "ensemble_price_usd": "Top-3 ensemble (USD)", "floor_p20_usd": "P20 (USD)",
        "ceiling_p80_usd": "P80 (USD)", "Spread": "Seller spread", "Frontier": "Pareto drop",
        "price_change_7d_pct": "7-day change (%)", "model_disagreement_pct": "Model spread (%)",
        "n_listings": "Listings", "Cheapest": "Cheapest at",
    }).round({"Gap (%)": 0, "Estimated typical (USD)": 0, "Top-3 ensemble (USD)": 0,
              "P20 (USD)": 0, "P80 (USD)": 0, "7-day change (%)": 1, "Model spread (%)": 1})
    return show(table, paging=True, pageLength=25, order=[[3, "asc"]], showIndex=False,
                classes="display compact", allow_html=True)


def summary(name, title):
    print(f"<summary>{icon(name)}<span>{title}</span>{icon('chev', 'fp-chev')}</summary>")
```

::: {.fp-detail-body}

Every candidate across linear (`OLS`, `Ridge`, `Lasso`, `ElasticNet`, `Bayesian Ridge`), robust
(`Huber`, `Theil-Sen`), quantile (`L1 Quantile P20 / P50 / P80`), tree/boosting (`Gradient
Boosted Trees L1 & Huber`, `Extra Trees`, `Random Forest`), local instance (`KNN`), and the
**`Weighted Ensemble (Top-3 LOO)`** is scored by leaving each part out in turn. Typical error is
the median absolute percentage error (MAPE) on the left-out parts.

<details class="fp-detail">

```{python}
#| output: asis
summary("info", "Method &amp; limitations")
```

::: {.fp-detail-body}

A **fair price** is the price a part would have if price followed its
[Blender benchmark](https://opendata.blender.org/) score and nothing else. The **gap** is how far
the lowest new listing is from that estimate: a negative gap means the part is cheap for the
rendering performance it delivers. A part within ±10% of its estimate reads as near fair.

The estimate for a part always comes from a fit that never saw that part. Eighteen models compete,
and a naive baseline (every part costs the same per point of score) is always on the leaderboard.
A model only replaces the baseline when it beats it by more than two standard errors.

**Model confidence** is the ensemble agreement: one minus the median spread between the top five
models' estimates. At 0.90 or more it reads High, at 0.80 or more Moderate, and Low below that.

**Market watch.** *Seller spread* is how far the cheapest listing sits below the median listing for
the same part, as a median over parts with two or more listings. *Frontier distance* is the median
price cut a part needs to match the cheapest rival that is at least as fast. *Price change* is the
median change in each part's lowest price across the last 30 days of collected history; until 30
days have been collected it covers the history so far, and the label says how many days.
*P20–P80 coverage* is the share of left-out parts whose price fell inside their P20–P80 band
(60% would be perfectly calibrated).

**Chart curves.** The P20–P80 band, the Top-3 ensemble line and the P50 regime curves are smooth
curves drawn through the per-part estimates in log–log space, so they show the shape of the fit.
The numbers for a part, in the detail cards and tables, are the model's own estimates for that part.

**Pareto drop** is the price cut needed to match the cheapest rival that is at least as fast. $0
means the part is already on the price–performance frontier.

A gap is a question, not an answer. Blender measures rendering only. A processor built for games,
or a graphics card with more memory, can cost more than its rendering score predicts and still be
priced sensibly. Graphics cards also run on different Blender backends, which favours NVIDIA, so
AMD and Intel cards look expensive here for that reason alone. Parts with a single listing appear in
the chart and tables but do not train the model, and their estimates carry low confidence.

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  const COLORS = { under: "#18b47b", near: "#f5b400", above: "#ef5b4c" };
  const usd = v => "$" + Math.round(v).toLocaleString("en-US");
  const graphOf = cat => cat.querySelector(".js-plotly-plot");

  document.querySelectorAll(".fp-cat").forEach(cat => {
    const pick = cat.querySelector(".fp-pick");
    if (!pick) return;
    const parts = JSON.parse(pick.dataset.parts);
    const select = pick.querySelector("select");
    const field = f => cat.querySelector(`[data-f="${f}"]`);

    const update = () => {
      const p = parts.find(d => d.name === select.value) || parts[0];
      const band = p.gap <= -10 ? "under" : p.gap >= 10 ? "above" : "near";
      const pill = band === "under" ? "fp-pill-neg" : band === "above" ? "fp-pill-pos" : "fp-pill-mod";
      const words = Math.abs(p.gap) < 0.5 ? "in line with estimate"
        : `${Math.abs(p.gap).toFixed(0)}% ${p.gap < 0 ? "below" : "above"} estimate`;
      pick.querySelector(".fp-pick-title").innerHTML =
        `${p.name} · ${usd(p.y)} listed · ${usd(p.est)} estimated typical · <span class="fp-pill ${pill}">${words}</span>`;
      pick.querySelector(".fp-pick-note").textContent = p.trusted
        ? `${p.n} listings · Estimate from a fit that left this part out.`
        : "One listing only · Low confidence (limited data; estimate may be less reliable).";
      field("pos").textContent = `${p.gap > 0 ? "+" : p.gap < 0 ? "−" : ""}${Math.abs(p.gap).toFixed(0)}%`;
      field("pos").classList.toggle("fp-neg", band === "above");
      field("range").textContent = `${usd(p.p20)} – ${usd(p.p80)}`;
      field("spread").textContent = p.spread;
      field("spread_note").textContent = p.spread_note;
      field("drop").textContent = usd(p.drop);
      field("drop_note").textContent = p.drop > 0
        ? `Cut needed to match ${p.rival || "a faster, cheaper part"}`
        : "Already on the price–performance frontier";

      const g = graphOf(cat);
      if (!g || !window.Plotly) return;
      const idx = g.data.findIndex(t => t.name === "selected");
      if (idx >= 0) Plotly.restyle(g, { x: [[p.x]], y: [[p.y]] }, [idx]);
      if (g.offsetWidth < 600) {
        // Phone width: the banner below carries the details, so skip the callout.
        Plotly.relayout(g, { annotations: [], "margin.l": 58, "margin.r": 8,
          "xaxis.title.text": "Blender score (log scale)", "yaxis.title.text": "Lowest new listing (USD)" });
        return;
      }
      Plotly.relayout(g, { annotations: [{
        x: Math.log10(p.x), y: Math.log10(p.y), xref: "x", yref: "y",
        ax: (Math.log10(p.x) - g.layout.xaxis.range[0]) / (g.layout.xaxis.range[1] - g.layout.xaxis.range[0]) < 0.5 ? 110 : -110,
        ay: (Math.log10(p.y) - g.layout.yaxis.range[0]) / (g.layout.yaxis.range[1] - g.layout.yaxis.range[0]) < 0.5 ? -100 : 90, showarrow: true, arrowhead: 2, arrowwidth: 1.5, arrowcolor: "#0f8f6c",
        align: "left", bgcolor: "rgba(255,255,255,0.96)", bordercolor: "#3fd4a0", borderwidth: 1.5, borderpad: 8,
        font: { color: "#14233a", size: 12 },
        text: `<b style="font-size:15px">${p.name}</b><br>${usd(p.y)} listed · ${usd(p.est)} estimated typical<br>` +
              `<b><span style="color:${COLORS[band]}">${words}</span></b><br>` +
              `<span style="color:#6b7a8c">${p.trusted ? p.n + " listings" : "One listing only · Low confidence"}</span>`,
      }] });
    };
    select.addEventListener("change", update);
    cat._fpUpdate = update;

    const g = graphOf(cat);
    if (g?.on) g.on("plotly_click", ev => {
      const name = ev.points?.[0]?.customdata?.[0];
      if (name && [...select.options].some(o => o.text === name)) { select.value = name; update(); }
    });

    cat.querySelectorAll(".fp-legend button[data-color]").forEach(btn => btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
      const mode = btn.dataset.color;
      cat.querySelectorAll(".fp-legend button[data-color]").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b === btn)));
      cat.querySelectorAll(".fp-legend ul[data-legend]").forEach(u => u.classList.toggle("fp-off", u.dataset.legend !== mode));
      const graph = graphOf(cat);
      if (!graph || !window.Plotly) return;
      const idx = [], vis = [];
      graph.data.forEach((t, i) => {
        if (t.name?.startsWith("gap:") || t.name?.startsWith("maker:")) { idx.push(i); vis.push(t.name.startsWith(mode + ":")); }
      });
      Plotly.restyle(graph, { visible: vis }, idx);
    }));
  });

  const show = kind => {
    document.querySelectorAll(".fp-tabs button").forEach(b => b.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(b.dataset.tab === kind)));
    document.querySelectorAll("[data-kind]").forEach(el => {
      el.style.setProperty("display", el.dataset.kind === kind ? (el.classList.contains("fp-watch") ? "grid" : "block") : "none", "important");
    });
    document.querySelectorAll(`.fp-cat[data-kind="${kind}"]`).forEach(cat => {
      const g = graphOf(cat);
      if (g && window.Plotly) Plotly.Plots.resize(g);
      cat._fpUpdate?.();
    });
  };
  document.querySelectorAll(".fp-tabs button").forEach(b => b.addEventListener("click", () => show(b.dataset.tab)));
  show("gpu");
  // Plotly may finish drawing after this script runs; refresh the callout once it has.
  const settle = () => document.querySelectorAll(".fp-cat").forEach(c => {
    const g = graphOf(c);
    if (g && g.offsetWidth && window.Plotly) Plotly.Plots.resize(g);
    c._fpUpdate?.();
  });
  setTimeout(settle, 300);
  window.addEventListener("load", settle);
});
</script>
